title: Marketplace vertical onboarding rubric and CTA bank
content:
Purpose
This doc is a practical rubric + creative bank for packaging Redwood Inference offerings by vertical (SaaS platform, internal developer platform, regulated enterprise). Use this during partner onboarding to speed up marketplace acceptance, reduce revision cycles, and standardize CTAs and tiles across cloud stores.

Scope
- Applies to publisher listing artifacts: tile title, short blurb, 2-line value props, hero bullets, CTAs, trial flow text, image/asset specs, SKU mapping notes, and the acceptance rubric used by GTM + Legal + Cloud QA.
- Not a replacement for legal billing docs or exact SKU numbers; those live in the billing appendix. This is the copy and acceptance checklist to get a listing published.

Quick intro checklist (minimum viable listing)
- Title fits 50 character limit (store-specific)
- Short description 1–2 lines, <140 characters
- Three hero bullets focused on value (latency, cost, deployment modes)
- CTA (trial or contact) variant selected
- Primary hero image in required dimensions and transparent background variant
- Privacy & compliance statement added (short form)
- SKU mapping noted and linked to billing ticket
- Acceptance rubric passed by Product, Legal, and Cloud QA

Acceptance rubric (go/no-go; score each row 0/1) - target >= 8/10 to publish
- Title: descriptive + includes either "Redwood Inference" or "Redwood" (1)
- Short blurb: technology + benefit present (1)
- Value bullets: customer benefit first, metric or example second (1)
- CTA: one obvious CTA present and correctly routed (trial, contact, or try-in-console) (1)
- Images: hero + thumbnail meet dimension & filetype (1)
- Legal blurb: includes data handling summary + link to full policy (1)
- SKU mapped or billing ticket open (1)
- Integration docs linked (Quickstart + SDK sample) (1)
- Performance claim caveats present (latency / throughput) if present (1)
- Acceptance tests: basic provisioning and billing flow documented (1)

Technical & asset requirements (store-agnostic checklist)
- Images: hero 1200x627 PNG or JPG; thumbnail 300x300 PNG; transparent variant for tile overlay recommended. Max 2MB per image.
- Logo: vector preferred, SVG or high-res PNG (min 600px width).
- Video: 30–45s demo clip optional; hosted on partner page or YouTube. Caption text required.
- Docs: Quickstart (3 steps) + REST sample + SDK snippet for Python/TS. Must be reachable in <2 clicks from listing.
- Trial flow: 14-day credit trial recommended; if not available, CTA must be "Contact Sales" and link to contact form with pre-filled product.
- Supported regions: list cloud regions where the product is available. If private deployments only, label clearly.

SKU mapping and trial variants (notes for ops)
- Default listing SKU: Redwood-Market-Hosted-API (maps to hosted usage-based plan).
- Dedicated SKU(s): Redwood-Dedicated-Reserve-{size} (tied to monthly commit).
- Private / On-prem SKU: Redwood-Private-Platform (requires separate procurement flow).
- Trial experiences: "Try in Console" should spin up a sandbox with token-limited quota. If the console demo is not feasible, default CTA must be "Request Trial" and route to presales.

Copy bank: Title variants (pick one and adapt to char limits)
- Redwood Inference — Production LLM serving for engineering teams
- High-performance LLM inference: hosted, dedicated, private
- Run and scale LLMs with predictable latency and cost

Short blurbs (<=140 chars)
- Production-grade inference for modern apps — low-latency, cost-aware serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Serve LLMs reliably at scale: streamlined rollout, cost controls, and built-in observability.

2-line value props (examples to use as bullets)
- Latency & throughput: <100ms median tail for common LLMs with autoscaling pools and smart routing.
- Cost control: batching, KV caching, and quantization recommendations to cut per-token costs by up to 4x.
- Deployment flexibility: same API for hosted, reserved, and private (VPC/on-prem) installs.
- Reliability: automated fallbacks and per-route SLAs to keep features live under load.

Hero bullets (short, benefit-first)
- Production-first API: fast onboarding + SDKs for Python/TS
- Predictable economics: usage + reserved capacity options
- Enterprise-ready: KMS, audit logs, and private control plane

CTA templates (select per listing)
- Primary CTA (try now): Start free trial — 14 days, credit-backed sandbox
- Secondary CTA (demo/contact): Contact sales for dedicated capacity and SLA
- Embedded CTA (developer): Try in console — run example in 30s (token-limited)
- Marketplace-specific CTA examples: "Launch trial", "Start 14-day sandbox", "Request procurement"

Suggested CTA routing rules
- If trial available: primary CTA -> sandbox provisioning flow; secondary -> presales contact form.
- If dedicated-only: primary CTA -> Request Sales (pre-filled template with SKU + company size)
- If private: CTA -> Schedule onboarding + compliance questionnaire link.

Performance & claims guidance (short form)
- Do not promise absolute latency without context: always include model family, sequence length, and region. Example: "~100–200ms median token latency on Llama2-70B in us-west-2 with batch=4".
- If referring to cost improvements, tie to a configured technique: "Up to 4x per-token cost reduction when using recommended KV caching and 4-bit quantization on dedicated pools."

Acceptance test scenarios (minimal automation suggestions)
- Provisioning smoke: click CTA -> creates sandbox project -> returns API key -> run a 3-step quickstart sample (OK response 200).
- Billing smoke: if trial consumes quota, ensure billing system records trial activation and mapping to default SKU.
- Console demo: example generation returns stream and final response; check streaming timeout < SLO.

Common rejection reasons & quick fixes
- Missing quickstart or unreachable docs: add GitHub README link and sample snippets.
- Unsupported trial promise: change CTA to contact sales or add sandbox.
- Images too large or wrong aspect ratio: supply hero and thumbnail per spec.
- Ambiguous data statements: add data handling blurb and link to full policy.

Handoff checklist for go-live
- GTM: confirm title + blurb + 3 bullets + CTA selected
- Design: upload hero, thumbnail, logo variants (SVG + PNG)
- Engineering: confirm provisioning hooks for trial + console demo
- Legal: approve short privacy blurb + billing mapping
- Cloud Ops: run provisioning acceptance tests and sign-off

Example tile copy (short/medium/long)
- Short (store tile): Redwood Inference — predictable, low-latency LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Medium (tile expanded): Redwood Inference helps engineering teams run LLMs in production with autoscaling, KV/prefix caching, quantization suggestions, and integrated observability. Try a 14-day sandbox.
- Long (listing page intro): Ship LLM-powered features with consistent performance and predictable costs. Redwood Inference combines a GPU-optimized serving runtime, smart routing, and deployment abstractions so your team can focus on product rather than ops. Available as Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private deployments (VPC/on-prem).

Notes & open questions (incomplete items to resolve before publish)
- Confirm the trial SKU and sandbox quota amounts (ops ticket open: GTM-4823).
- Decide whether to include a 30s demo video on the tile; design estimate required.
- Need Legal sign-off on the short privacy text for EU marketplace variant.

Quick references and shortcuts
- Copy owner: Asha Patel (GTM) — use this doc as the source of truth for copy iterations.
- Design lead: Riley Chen — asset uploads and aspect checks.
- Engineering contact: Diego Morales — trial provisioning hooks and console demo.
- Related tickets: JIRA GTM-4823 (billing mapping), JIRA PLAT-6110 (trial sandbox infra).

Appendix: short privacy blurb (store-ready)
- We process usage data to deliver and optimize inference; we do not train models on customer input. See full data policy at: https://redwood.ai/legal/data-policy

End of doc — use this as the shared template for vertical onboarding; copy freely but keep the acceptance rubric intact.
